hyperedges.label: Kind Metadata Table Drives Record, Category and Dashboard Surfaces
Orphan-Safe Category Lifecycle (Other fallback, no cascade, no rewrite)
Firestore Rules as the Sole Security Boundary

nodes.label: Non-negotiable Rules
nodes.rationale: Guardrails keeping the app serverless, uid-scoped, secret-free and non-destructive: no server/Cloud Function/Admin SDK/service account, no stored totals/net worth/splits/counts, no access outside users/{uid}/, no committed .env.local, no cascade delete or record rewrite on category change, preserve the donut palette, justify every new dependency, no unrelated refactors.

nodes.label: Firestore Security Requirements and Review
nodes.rationale: Rules must require request.auth != null and request.auth.uid == uid and deny all other documents/users; any change to Auth, Firestore paths or rules must be reviewed against docs/firebase-security.md to verify no cross-user read or write is possible.

nodes.label: Pure Derived-Logic Selectors
nodes.rationale: Totals, net worth, record/category counts, bucket splits and resolved names (unresolved IDs -> Other) are computed by pure selectors or utilities instead of being stored; investment amounts count negative in net worth.

nodes.label: Shared Kind-Metadata Architecture
nodes.rationale: One metadata table drives record routes, record forms, category panels, dashboard selectors and chart labels so three record pages are never duplicated and a new kind needs only one metadata entry plus its route.

nodes.label: Centralized Firebase Access and Path Construction
nodes.norm_label: centralized firebase access and path construction

nodes.label: UI-Boundary Write Validation
nodes.rationale: Amount, UTC date, notes length and name checks run before every write to improve UX; client validation is explicitly not security and Firestore rules remain the security boundary.

nodes.label: Snapshot Listener Lifecycle and Loading State
nodes.rationale: Six onSnapshot listeners mount after sign-in and are unsubscribed on sign-out and effect cleanup; snapshots rather than local writes are authoritative, and auth/collection loading is explicit so a legitimate zero is never rendered before the first snapshot.
nodes.norm_label: snapshot listener lifecycle and loading state

nodes.label: UI Rules
nodes.rationale: Accessible presentation: skeletons instead of zero while loading, tabular-nums only in table columns, signed net worth so colour is never the only cue, preserved light/dark donut palette and surfaces, chart table fallback, no categorical chart colour as text.

nodes.label: Build and Deploy Commands
nodes.rationale: npm run build after meaningful changes; firebase deploy only when the user explicitly asks.

nodes.label: MyExpenseLog
nodes.rationale: Personal finance ledger for one signed-in user logging income, expenditure and investments; net worth is derived, never stored.

nodes.label: Net Worth Formula (Sum income - Sum expenditure - Sum investments)
nodes.rationale: Derived on every render from the three record totals and never cached or stored (Core decisions).
nodes.norm_label: net worth formula (sum income - sum expenditure - sum investments)

nodes.label: users/{uid} Data Model
nodes.rationale: Three record collections plus three category collections instead of one transactions table, because income uses sources while expenditure and investment use categories (different vocabulary).

nodes.label: UTC-Midnight ISO Dates
nodes.rationale: Dates stored as UTC-midnight ISO strings so month/year bucketing is timezone-safe.

nodes.label: Case-Insensitive Name Uniqueness per Collection
nodes.rationale: Names are trimmed, 1-40 chars and unique case-insensitively only within their own collection, so 'Salary' may exist as both an income source and an expense category; enforced client-side as UX, not by rules.

nodes.label: "Other" Read-Time Label
nodes.rationale: Other is never a document; null and unresolvable category/source IDs fall back to it at read time, so deleting a category can never orphan or corrupt a record and nothing is rewritten.

nodes.label: Kind Metadata Table
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth (label, records collection, category collection, FK field, category noun, sign +1/-1) driving the record page, category page and dashboard; a 4th kind costs one row plus one route.

nodes.label: Generic Record Page
nodes.rationale: One page serves income, expenditure and investment via the metadata table instead of three near-identical pages.

nodes.label: Categories Page (/category)
nodes.rationale: One route with three metadata-driven panels (tabs on mobile, columns at lg) for all category collections, because three near-identical pages would drift; the only place categories are created.

nodes.label: Category Rename via Doc-ID Reference
nodes.rationale: Records reference the category doc id, so renaming relabels every record and chart slice on the next snapshot with no data migration.

nodes.label: Non-Cascading Category Delete
nodes.rationale: deleteDoc touches no records; their FK becomes unresolvable and renders as Other, so a delete can never destroy or corrupt a record. The confirm dialog states the affected record count.

nodes.label: Dashboard (/)
nodes.rationale: Every number is derived at render time from the shared Redux slices; nothing is cached or stored.

nodes.label: Stat Cards
nodes.rationale: Net worth is the hero card and always carries a sign character so meaning is never colour-alone; cards use proportional figures, tabular-nums is reserved for tables.

nodes.label: Skeleton Before First Snapshot
nodes.rationale: Cards show a skeleton until the first snapshot lands and only then render a real 0 (not a dash), so loading is never shown as zero.

nodes.label: Fixed Donut Colour Palette
nodes.rationale: Eight fixed slots, never cycled, keyed to category createdAt order rather than slice rank so sorting or filtering never repaints survivors; 9th+ categories fold into Other (muted grey #898781, not a slot); explicit dark column rather than auto flip; surfaces #fcfcfb/#1a1a19; text stays in ink tokens.

nodes.label: Donut Table-View Fallback
nodes.rationale: A toggle renders each donut as a two-column table: the accessibility fallback and required relief for any sub-3:1 colour on the light surface.

nodes.label: Zero-Value Categories Not Drawn
nodes.rationale: A category with no records would be invisible 0% geometry with a live legend entry, so such categories are listed under the chart as 'N categories with no records yet'.

nodes.label: Auth-to-Redux Snapshot Data Flow
nodes.rationale: Six listeners (three record, three category collections) mount together so /category edits and dashboard charts update from the same Firestore echo with no refetch; writes go straight to Firestore.

nodes.label: Redux Slices (one per collection + auth)
nodes.rationale: Totals and splits are selectors, never stored in state.

nodes.label: Firestore Security Rules (owner-only users/{uid}/**)
nodes.rationale: With no server, rules are the only access control: read/write only when request.auth.uid == uid, everything else denied; rules intentionally do not validate document shape (client validator's job, UX not security).

nodes.label: No-Server Architecture (Firebase free tier)
nodes.rationale: Free tier only with no server or Cloud Functions, which makes Firestore Security Rules the sole access-control layer.

nodes.label: Firebase Project Setup
nodes.rationale: Rules are deployed before real data lands.

nodes.label: firebase.json Hosting and Rules Config
nodes.rationale: Hosting serves dist with an SPA rewrite of every path to /index.html so client-side routes resolve; firestore section points at firestore.rules and firestore.indexes.json.

nodes.label: Firebase Security Guide
nodes.rationale: Goal is to move from simple rule generation to a security-first engineering process.

nodes.label: Security-First Workflow
nodes.rationale: Four steps: codebase analysis of queries/models/auth, least-privilege implementation, devil's-advocate attack, and validation before any deployment.

nodes.label: Rule Validator Helper Functions (isValidUser())
nodes.rationale: Helper functions keep rule checks consistent.

nodes.label: Devil's Advocate Rule Attack
nodes.rationale: Systematically tries to break rules via public list exploits, ownership hijacking (changing the UID in a request) and resource exhaustion (mass small-document creation for DoS).

nodes.label: MyExpenseLog Security Rule Requirements
nodes.rationale: Every query scoped to users/{uid}; deny root and other user subtrees; no secret or service-account credentials ever stored in the frontend.

nodes.label: Rule-Validated Writes (amount, date)
nodes.rationale: Asks rules to ensure amount is a finite number > 0 and date is a valid ISO string; this conflicts with project-spec, whose rules deliberately do not validate document shape.

nodes.label: Testing Guide
nodes.rationale: Logic verification is mandatory and runs against the Firebase Local Emulator Suite before any production deploy.

nodes.label: Bug-Fix Regression Test Policy
nodes.rationale: Every bug fix must include a test case that previously failed and now passes.

nodes.label: Minimal Test Setup (node:test / assert)
nodes.rationale: No heavy test frameworks unless explicitly requested.

nodes.label: React Compiler (disabled)
nodes.rationale: Not enabled because of its impact on dev and build performance.
